doc.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Advice to students: keep listening
summary: Gitler urges students to listen widely, with the Slam Stewart anecdote leading a friend to Parker and Dizzy, and to use critics only as guides.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Yeah, I wanted to ask you perhaps maybe just one last question here and that is you know students hopefully, the students even at our college and perhaps even other colleges, will see these tapes. Tell us a few things that students should know about jazz, other than just the names and dates.

Well the names and dates are things that you latch on to once you get interested in a particular band or a particular musician and so you want to know when this happened, how it happened, etcetera, etcetera. But I think the thing to do is keep your ears open and listen, and listen as much as you can. And the more you listen, the more knowledgeable you become and the more sophisticated in your listening, and you’re able to make judgments and comparisons, and also to understand your taste. Because everyone’s taste is different, but you kind of begin to see what you like more and one recording may lead

you to another and then it’s like I had a friend who liked jazz but he wasn’t avidly as into it as myself, and he took Slam Stewart — he loved Slam Stewart singing and bowing the bass at the same time. Everybody kind of could get with that. And because he liked Slam and I played the record of “Groovin’ High” which I spoke of before for him, and Slam plays on that. So he bought that because of Slam. And then he said to me, “Wow, Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie.” So Slam Stewart really opened that other thing up for him. And you know, just keep your ears open and listen, and as we used to say reading movie criticism when we were teenagers, after you get to know your critics, the same thing in jazz, you know what to expect from them and you know when and who will say something that you can rely on. But you have to use your own ears basically, just use that as a guide. You know you have to listen for yourself. The more you listen the more you know and the more you’ll enjoy it.
